disclosures.said: Only the solid coloured boxes that carry a tag are things I am asking about. The thin dashed lines you may see on some pictures are marks left over in the pictures themselves; disregard them.
About screen 24: that picture was taken before the middle of the page had finished drawing; on the running app that middle area shows the same thing as on screen 8.
(there is no 13 and no 29 for you — skip those numbers)

screen1-a1.where: Top right of the header, the left one of two pictures next to the title 'PDF Reader'.
screen1-a1.expectation: I think it opens something about paying for a premium version. A crown is not a function, it is an idea of 'royal' or 'best', so I am inferring 'premium' from it.
screen1-a1.cue: Only the picture of a gold crown. There is no text next to it.

first_pass.why: A crown does not depict an action. I have to translate a symbol into 'upgrade' or 'premium', and I could be wrong; it could also be an award, a ranking, or a profile badge.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Premium' or 'Upgrade' under or next to the crown, the way the Settings screen does with 'Upgrade to Premium'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown picture at the top right. Look at what opens (do NOT press "Start Free Trial"). Then close that page with the X at its top left, and look at the crown again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a short delay a full-screen page opened. Its heading is 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. It lists what Premium gives (remove ads, unlock all features, high-quality PDF scans), then '3 day free trial, then $29.99/year' and a 'Start Free Trial' button, which I did not press. The picture at the top of that page is a diamond, not a crown. I closed it with the X at the top left and was back on the main page, where the crown looks exactly the same as before, still with no word next to it.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: Pressing it answered the question once: it is the Premium offer. But the crown itself still says nothing, and the page it opens shows a diamond, not a crown, so there is not even a visual link between the two. I know it now because I pressed it, not because the picture told me. It needs the word 'Premium'.

screen1-a2.where: Top right of the header, the right-most picture, next to the crown.
screen1-a2.expectation: Probably opens Settings. But the picture is a gear with a wrench through it, and the bottom bar also has an item called 'Tools', so it could also be tools or maintenance.
screen1-a2.cue: Only the gear-and-wrench picture. No text.

first_pass.why: A plain gear I would read as settings. A gear plus a wrench is two symbols combined, and 'wrench' literally means tools. With a 'Tools' tab on the same screen I cannot be sure which one this is.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'Settings' in text, or use a plain gear only, so it does not overlap with the 'Tools' tab.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the gear-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' and a '<' back arrow, listing Upgrade to Premium, Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader, Add widget, Rate App, Share App, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use. I went back to the main page. Then I pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. It opened a different page with the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' and tiles such as Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF, Merge PDF and Watermark. So the gear is settings and the Tools tab is the tools. They are two different places.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: The gear opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and 'Tools' opens the tool list. They are two different places, and each is named where it lands. The spanner on the gear is still unnecessary, but my worry that the gear might be the tools does not hold.

screen1-a8.where: Left end of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very small grey 'x' in the top corner and a book picture beside it.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing that corner simply closes the strip, whichever part you touch

The whole grey 'Set as default reader' strip disappeared and the page closed up underneath it. Nothing else opened; I took a second screenshot to be sure. The strip was gone, so I could not press the x in the same session. I restarted the app to get the strip back and pressed the x in G3-T2.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: After restarting the app (I closed the Google Play 'update' page with its X and pressed 'Continue to app' on the advert), the strip was back. I pressed the tiny x at its far left. The strip disappeared and nothing else happened; the rest of the page stayed as it was. So the book and the x do exactly the same thing: they close the strip.

screen1-a8.closing_comment: The book and the x both just close the strip, and nothing else happens. The whole corner is one close target, so it does not matter which part I press. The x is still tiny and faint, but that is a visibility issue, not a question of what it does.
